#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
ENV_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/.env"

if [[ -f "$ENV_FILE" ]]; then
  echo ".env already exists. Refusing to overwrite it."
  echo "Delete .env yourself if you intentionally want to regenerate local secrets."
  echo "Regenerating .env also requires wiping Docker volumes because Postgres, MinIO, Temporal, and SpiceDB persist credentials."
  exit 1
fi

umask 077

secret() {
  openssl rand -base64 32 | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '='
}

uuid() {
  local hex
  hex="$(openssl rand -hex 16)"
  echo "${hex:0:8}-${hex:8:4}-4${hex:13:3}-a${hex:17:3}-${hex:20:12}"
}

prompt_default() {
  local prompt="$1"
  local default="$2"
  local value
  read -r -p "$prompt [$default]: " value
  echo "${value:-$default}"
}

prompt_required() {
  local prompt="$1"
  local value
  while true; do
    read -r -p "$prompt: " value
    if [[ -n "$value" ]]; then
      echo "$value"
      return
    fi
    echo "Value is required." >&2
  done
}

prompt_optional() {
  local prompt="$1"
  local value
  read -r -p "$prompt: " value
  echo "$value"
}

prompt_secret() {
  local prompt="$1"
  local value
  while true; do
    read -r -s -p "$prompt: " value
    echo >&2
    if [[ -n "$value" ]]; then
      echo "$value"
      return
    fi
    echo "Value is required." >&2
  done
}

prompt_optional_secret() {
  local prompt="$1"
  local value
  read -r -s -p "$prompt: " value
  echo >&2
  echo "$value"
}

echo "Creating $ENV_FILE"
echo "These values are shared local secrets. Keep .env ignored and private."
echo "If you regenerate this file later, wipe Docker volumes before restarting the stack."
echo

local_user_email="$(prompt_default "Login email for the local Keycloak user" "spark@example.com")"
local_user_password="$(prompt_secret "Login password for the local Keycloak user")"
local_user_first_name="$(prompt_default "First name of the local Keycloak user" "Spark")"
local_user_last_name="$(prompt_default "Last name of the local Keycloak user" "User")"
local_user_id="$(uuid)"

litellm_base_url="$(prompt_required "LiteLLM/OpenAI-compatible base URL")"
litellm_master_key="$(prompt_secret "LiteLLM master key")"
litellm_text_model="$(prompt_required "LiteLLM chat model")"
litellm_embedding_model="$(prompt_required "LiteLLM embedding model")"
litellm_visual_model="$(prompt_required "LiteLLM vision/multimodal model (image + PDF-page analysis, e.g. for Inhaltsextraktion)")"

docling_protocol="$(prompt_default "Docling protocol" "https")"
docling_host="$(prompt_required "Docling host")"
docling_port="$(prompt_default "Docling port" "443")"
docling_ocr_engine="$(prompt_default "Docling OCR engine" "easyocr")"
docling_token_url="$(prompt_optional "Docling OAuth token URL (leave empty for unauthenticated Docling)")"
docling_client_id="$(prompt_optional "Docling OAuth client ID (leave empty for unauthenticated Docling)")"
docling_client_secret="$(prompt_optional_secret "Docling OAuth client secret (leave empty for unauthenticated Docling)")"
docling_base_url="${docling_protocol}://${docling_host}"
if [[ "$docling_port" != "80" && "$docling_port" != "443" ]]; then
  docling_base_url="${docling_base_url}:${docling_port}"
fi

db_password="$(secret)"
s3_access_key_id="spark-local-$(openssl rand -hex 4)"
s3_secret_access_key="$(secret)"
spicedb_token="$(secret)"
keycloak_bootstrap_admin_password="$(secret)"
local_keycloak_client_secret="$(secret)"
oauth2_proxy_cookie_secret="$(secret)"
injection_model_token="$(secret)"

# Browser-facing base URLs.
# When WEB_HOST is set, the stack runs behind a reverse proxy that publishes every port at
# https://<port>-$WEB_HOST and authenticates requests, blocking cross-origin CORS preflight. So
# in that case we (a) point every browser-facing URL at the public host and (b) serve object
# storage same-origin through the frontend (oauth2-proxy) instead of a separate MinIO port, so
# uploads/downloads are not cross-origin. Locally we keep plain localhost and direct MinIO.
# WEB_HOST is not always inherited by non-login shells, so fall back to PID 1's environment.
web_host="${WEB_HOST:-$(tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/1/environ 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^WEB_HOST=//p')}"
if [[ -n "$web_host" ]]; then
  frontend_public_url="https://3000-${web_host}"
  keycloak_public_url="https://9090-${web_host}"
  # Same-origin as the frontend: presigned URLs are served via oauth2-proxy's /dms-local/ route.
  s3_public_url="https://3000-${web_host}"
  temporal_ui_public_url="https://8233-${web_host}"
  cookie_secure="true"
  echo "Detected reverse-proxy deployment (WEB_HOST=$web_host); using public https://<port>-\$WEB_HOST URLs."
else
  frontend_public_url="http://localhost:3000"
  keycloak_public_url="http://localhost:9090"
  s3_public_url="http://localhost:9000"
  temporal_ui_public_url="http://localhost:8233"
  cookie_secure="false"
fi

cat > "$ENV_FILE" <<EOF
# Generated by scripts/create_secrets.sh. Do not commit this file.

# Shared local infrastructure secrets
DB_PASSWORD=$db_password
S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID=$s3_access_key_id
S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=$s3_secret_access_key
AUTH_SPICE_DB_TOKEN=$spicedb_token
KEYCLOAK_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD=$keycloak_bootstrap_admin_password
LOCAL_KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET=$local_keycloak_client_secret
OAUTH2_PROXY_COOKIE_SECRET=$oauth2_proxy_cookie_secret
INJECTION_MODEL_TOKEN=$injection_model_token

# Browser-facing base URLs. Localhost by default, or https://<port>-\$WEB_HOST behind
# a reverse proxy. Consumed by docker-compose.yaml (Keycloak hostname + oauth2-proxy) and
# process-compose.yaml (frontend). Regenerate .env after switching between plain-localhost and reverse-proxy setups.
FRONTEND_PUBLIC_URL=$frontend_public_url
KEYCLOAK_PUBLIC_URL=$keycloak_public_url
S3_PUBLIC_URL=$s3_public_url
TEMPORAL_UI_PUBLIC_URL=$temporal_ui_public_url
OAUTH2_PROXY_COOKIE_SECURE=$cookie_secure

# Local Keycloak login user (seeded by the keycloak-bootstrap container)
LOCAL_USER_ID=$local_user_id
LOCAL_USER_EMAIL=$local_user_email
LOCAL_USER_PASSWORD=$local_user_password
LOCAL_USER_FIRST_NAME=$local_user_first_name
LOCAL_USER_LAST_NAME=$local_user_last_name

# External LiteLLM-compatible endpoint
LITELLM_BASE_URL=$litellm_base_url
LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=$litellm_master_key
LITELLM_TEXT_MODEL=$litellm_text_model
LITELLM_EMBEDDING_MODEL=$litellm_embedding_model
LITELLM_VISUAL_MODEL=$litellm_visual_model

# External Docling endpoint
DOCLING_PROTOCOL=$docling_protocol
DOCLING_HOST=$docling_host
DOCLING_PORT=$docling_port
DOCLING_BASE_URL=$docling_base_url
DOCLING_OCR_ENGINE=$docling_ocr_engine
DOCLING_TIMEOUT=600
EOF

# Empty values break URL validation in workers, so only write the Docling
# OAuth settings when Docling actually requires OAuth.
if [[ -n "$docling_token_url" ]]; then
  printf 'DOCLING_TOKEN_URL=%s\nDOCLING_CLIENT_ID=%s\nDOCLING_CLIENT_SECRET=%s\n' \
    "$docling_token_url" "$docling_client_id" "$docling_client_secret" >> "$ENV_FILE"
fi

chmod 600 "$ENV_FILE"
echo "Created $ENV_FILE"

# Local infrastructure for native development.
# Runtime Python services are started with process-compose.yaml.
services:
  postgresql:
    image: pgvector/pgvector:pg16
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - postgresql_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      - ./scripts/data/gesetze-normen-seed.sql.gz:/seed/gesetze-normen-seed.sql.gz:ro
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: postgres
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD}
      POSTGRES_DB: postgres
    configs:
      - source: postgresql_init_sql
        target: /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/init.sql
      - source: postgresql_seed_gesetze_normen
        target: /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/seed-gesetze-normen.sh
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U postgres -d postgres"]
      interval: 3s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 30

  temporal:
    image: temporalio/auto-setup:1.29.0
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "7233:7233"
    volumes:
      - ./docker/temporal/development-sql.yaml:/etc/temporal/config/dynamicconfig/development-sql.yaml
    environment:
      DB: postgres12
      DB_PORT: 5432
      POSTGRES_USER: postgres
      POSTGRES_PWD: ${DB_PASSWORD}
      POSTGRES_SEEDS: postgresql
      DYNAMIC_CONFIG_FILE_PATH: config/dynamicconfig/development-sql.yaml
      BIND_ON_IP: 0.0.0.0
      TEMPORAL_ADDRESS: 0.0.0.0:7233
      TEMPORAL_CLI_ADDRESS: 0.0.0.0:7233
    depends_on:
      postgresql:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "tctl", "--address", "temporal:7233", "cluster", "h"]
      interval: 2s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 60

  temporal-init:
    image: temporalio/admin-tools:1.29
    depends_on:
      temporal:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      TEMPORAL_ADDRESS: temporal:7233
      TEMPORAL_CLI_ADDRESS: temporal:7233
    restart: "no"
    entrypoint:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - |
        set -eu
        until temporal operator cluster health --address temporal:7233 | grep -q SERVING; do
          echo "Waiting for Temporal server to start..."
          sleep 1
        done

        until temporal operator search-attribute list --address temporal:7233 --namespace default >/dev/null 2>&1; do
          echo "Waiting for namespace cache to refresh..."
          sleep 1
        done

        temporal operator search-attribute create --address temporal:7233 --namespace default --name ProjectId --type Keyword || true
        temporal operator search-attribute create --address temporal:7233 --namespace default --name ProjectVersion --type Int || true
        echo "Project search attributes registered."
        temporal operator namespace update --address temporal:7233 --namespace default --retention 60d
        tail -f /dev/null

  temporal-ui:
    image: temporalio/ui:2.44.1
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "8233:8080"
    depends_on:
      temporal:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      TEMPORAL_ADDRESS: temporal:7233

  minio:
    image: minio/minio
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "9000:9000"
      - "9001:9001"
    volumes:
      - minio_data:/data
    environment:
      MINIO_ROOT_USER: ${S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID}
      MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}
    command: server /data --console-address ":9001"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -fsS http://localhost:9000/minio/health/live >/dev/null"]
      interval: 3s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 30

  minio-init:
    image: minio/mc
    depends_on:
      minio:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID}
      S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}
      DMS_BUCKET_NAME: dms-local
      TEMPORAL_S3_BUCKET_NAME: temporal-payloads
      QUARANTINE_BUCKET_NAME: quarantine-bucket
    restart: "no"
    entrypoint:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - |
        set -eu
        mc alias set local http://minio:9000 "$$S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID" "$$S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"
        mc mb -p "local/$$DMS_BUCKET_NAME" || true
        mc mb -p "local/$$TEMPORAL_S3_BUCKET_NAME" || true
        mc mb -p "local/$$QUARANTINE_BUCKET_NAME" || true
        tail -f /dev/null

  minio-proxy:
    # Host-restoring reverse proxy in front of MinIO for presigned URLs. An authenticating
    # reverse proxy may rewrite the inbound Host (real host -> X-Forwarded-Host), which would make
    # MinIO reject SigV4 presigned URLs with 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch. This sidecar restores
    # Host from X-Forwarded-Host before MinIO validates the signature. See
    # docker/minio-proxy/nginx.conf. Reached only over the compose network (via oauth2-proxy).
    image: nginx:1.27-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      minio:
        condition: service_healthy
    volumes:
      - ./docker/minio-proxy/nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf:ro

  qdrant:
    image: qdrant/qdrant:v1.17.1
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "6333:6333"
      - "6334:6334"
    ulimits:
      nofile:
        soft: 65536
        hard: 65536
    volumes:
      - qdrant_data:/qdrant/storage

  tempo:
    image: grafana/tempo:2.9.0
    profiles: ["observability"]

  loki:

  otel-collector:

    depends_on:

  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:v3.4.2
    profiles: ["observability"]
    command:

    volumes:

      - prometheus_data:/prometheus
    ports:

    extra_hosts:

  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana-oss:11.2.0
    profiles: ["observability"]

      - grafana_data:/var/lib/grafana
    depends_on:
      - tempo
      - loki
      - prometheus

  keycloak:
    image: quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.0
    command:
      - start-dev
      - --http-port=9090
    environment:
      KC_DB: dev-file
      # Public base URL of Keycloak as the browser reaches it: http://localhost:9090 locally,
      # https://9090-$WEB_HOST behind a reverse proxy. This drives the token `iss`, so it must
      # match OAUTH2_PROXY_OIDC_ISSUER_URL. STRICT=false still lets internal callers (oauth2-proxy
      # token redeem, the bootstrap container) reach Keycloak on the docker network at keycloak:9090.
      KC_HOSTNAME: ${KEYCLOAK_PUBLIC_URL:-http://localhost:9090}
      KC_HOSTNAME_STRICT: false
      KC_HTTP_ENABLED: true
      # Honour X-Forwarded-* from the TLS-terminating reverse proxy (no-op locally).
      KC_PROXY_HEADERS: xforwarded
      KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_USERNAME: admin
      KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${KEYCLOAK_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD}
      KC_FEATURES: token-exchange
      KC_HEALTH_ENABLED: true
    ports:
      - "9090:9090"
    healthcheck:
      test:
        [
          "CMD-SHELL",
          "bash -ec 'exec 3<>/dev/tcp/localhost/9000; printf \"GET /health/ready HTTP/1.0\\r\\n\\r\\n\" >&3; head -n 1 <&3 | grep -q \"200\"'",
        ]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 30

  keycloak-bootstrap:
    image: quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.0
    depends_on:
      keycloak:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      KEYCLOAK_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${KEYCLOAK_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD}
      LOCAL_KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET: ${LOCAL_KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET}
      LOCAL_USER_ID: ${LOCAL_USER_ID}
      LOCAL_USER_EMAIL: ${LOCAL_USER_EMAIL}
      LOCAL_USER_PASSWORD: ${LOCAL_USER_PASSWORD}
      LOCAL_USER_FIRST_NAME: ${LOCAL_USER_FIRST_NAME}
      LOCAL_USER_LAST_NAME: ${LOCAL_USER_LAST_NAME}
      # Used to register the OIDC client's redirectUris / webOrigins (see bootstrap.sh).
      FRONTEND_PUBLIC_URL: ${FRONTEND_PUBLIC_URL:-http://localhost:3000}
    restart: on-failure
    volumes:
      - ./docker/keycloak/bootstrap.sh:/bootstrap.sh:ro
    entrypoint: ["/bin/bash", "/bootstrap.sh"]

  oauth2-proxy:
    image: quay.io/oauth2-proxy/oauth2-proxy:v7.8.1
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "3000:4180"
    depends_on:
      keycloak-bootstrap:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    environment:
      OAUTH2_PROXY_HTTP_ADDRESS: 0.0.0.0:4180
      # Default upstream is the frontend dev server (runs on the host via process-compose).
      # The extra /dms-local/ route serves MinIO same-origin so browser uploads/downloads avoid
      # cross-origin CORS preflight, which an authenticating reverse proxy blocks. MinIO uses
      # path-style addressing and SigV4 signs the Host header. An authenticating reverse proxy may
      # rewrite the inbound Host (the real host is moved to X-Forwarded-Host) before oauth2-proxy
      # sees it; PASS_HOST_HEADER would then forward that wrong Host to MinIO and presigned URLs
      # fail with 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch. So /dms-local/* is routed through the minio-proxy
      # sidecar, which restores Host from X-Forwarded-Host before MinIO validates the signature.
      # Longest-prefix wins, so /dms-local/* goes to minio-proxy and everything else to the
      # frontend. Add one route per additional browser-facing bucket.
      OAUTH2_PROXY_UPSTREAMS: http://host.docker.internal:3002,http://minio-proxy:9000/dms-local/
      # Trust X-Forwarded-* from the reverse proxy (no-op on plain localhost).
      OAUTH2_PROXY_REVERSE_PROXY: "true"
      OAUTH2_PROXY_PROVIDER: keycloak-oidc
      OAUTH2_PROXY_CLIENT_ID: local-client
      OAUTH2_PROXY_CLIENT_SECRET: ${LOCAL_KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET}
      OAUTH2_PROXY_COOKIE_SECRET: ${OAUTH2_PROXY_COOKIE_SECRET}
      # true under HTTPS (behind a reverse proxy), false for plain-http localhost.
      OAUTH2_PROXY_COOKIE_SECURE: ${OAUTH2_PROXY_COOKIE_SECURE:-false}
      OAUTH2_PROXY_EMAIL_DOMAINS: "*"
      OAUTH2_PROXY_REDIRECT_URL: ${FRONTEND_PUBLIC_URL:-http://localhost:3000}/oauth2/callback
      OAUTH2_PROXY_SKIP_PROVIDER_BUTTON: "true"
      OAUTH2_PROXY_CODE_CHALLENGE_METHOD: S256
      # Browser-facing (front-channel) Keycloak URLs use the public host; the back-channel
      # (redeem/jwks/profile) stays on the docker network and never traverses the reverse
      # proxy. OIDC discovery cannot express that split, so the endpoints are set explicitly.
      OAUTH2_PROXY_SKIP_OIDC_DISCOVERY: "true"
      OAUTH2_PROXY_OIDC_ISSUER_URL: ${KEYCLOAK_PUBLIC_URL:-http://localhost:9090}/realms/local
      OAUTH2_PROXY_LOGIN_URL: ${KEYCLOAK_PUBLIC_URL:-http://localhost:9090}/realms/local/protocol/openid-connect/auth
      OAUTH2_PROXY_REDEEM_URL: http://keycloak:9090/realms/local/protocol/openid-connect/token
      OAUTH2_PROXY_OIDC_JWKS_URL: http://keycloak:9090/realms/local/protocol/openid-connect/certs
      OAUTH2_PROXY_PROFILE_URL: http://keycloak:9090/realms/local/protocol/openid-connect/userinfo
    extra_hosts:
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"

  spicedb:
    image: authzed/spicedb:v1.49.0
    container_name: spicedb
    command: >
      serve
      --datastore-engine=memory
      --grpc-preshared-key=${AUTH_SPICE_DB_TOKEN}
    environment:
      ZED_TOKEN: ${AUTH_SPICE_DB_TOKEN}
    healthcheck:
      test: [ "CMD", "grpc_health_probe", "-addr=:50051" ]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10
    ports:
      - "50051:50051"

configs:
  # Loads the public gesetze-normen seed (deconstructed norms) on first
  # database initialization. Runs after init.sql created the databases.
  postgresql_seed_gesetze_normen:
    content: |
      echo "Seeding the gesetze-normen database from /seed/gesetze-normen-seed.sql.gz"
      # sed drops pg_dump 17 statements that PostgreSQL 16 does not know:
      # the \restrict guard and the transaction_timeout setting.
      gunzip -c /seed/gesetze-normen-seed.sql.gz \
        | sed -e '/^\\restrict /d' -e '/^\\unrestrict /d' -e '/^SET transaction_timeout/d' \
        | psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 --username "$$POSTGRES_USER" --dbname gesetze-normen
      echo "Finished seeding the gesetze-normen database"

  postgresql_init_sql:
    content: |
      SELECT 'CREATE DATABASE temporal'
      WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_database WHERE datname = 'temporal')\gexec

      WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_database WHERE datname = 'spicedb')\gexec

      SELECT 'CREATE DATABASE diplan'
      WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_database WHERE datname = 'diplan')\gexec
      SELECT 'CREATE DATABASE comment_service_db'
      WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_database WHERE datname = 'comment_service_db')\gexec
      SELECT 'CREATE DATABASE feedback_db'
      WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_database WHERE datname = 'feedback_db')\gexec
      SELECT 'CREATE DATABASE objections_db'
      WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_database WHERE datname = 'objections_db')\gexec
      SELECT 'CREATE DATABASE identity_management_db'
      WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_database WHERE datname = 'identity_management_db')\gexec
      SELECT 'CREATE DATABASE supplementary_requests'
      WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_database WHERE datname = 'supplementary_requests')\gexec
      SELECT 'CREATE DATABASE fpp'
      WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_database WHERE datname = 'fpp')\gexec
      SELECT 'CREATE DATABASE "gesetze-normen"'
      WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_database WHERE datname = 'gesetze-normen')\gexec
      SELECT 'CREATE DATABASE "begruendungen-db"'

# Native runtime services for local development.
# Start shared infrastructure first with:
#   docker compose --env-file .env up --wait
version: "0.5"

environment:
  - ENV=dev
  - AUTH_MODE=disabled
  - PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
  - DB_USER=postgres
  - DB_PASSWORD=${DB_PASSWORD}
  - DB_HOST=localhost
  - DB_PORT=5432
  - TEMPORAL_JOB_SERVICE_URL=http://localhost:18015
  - TEMPORAL_HOST=localhost:7233
  - TEMPORAL_SERVER_URL=localhost:7233
  - TEMPORAL_ADDRESS=localhost:7233
  - TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE=default
  - TEMPORAL_S3_BUCKET_NAME=temporal-payloads
  - TEMPORAL_S3_ENDPOINT_URL=http://localhost:9000
  - TEMPORAL_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID=${S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID}
  - TEMPORAL_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=${S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}
  - TEMPORAL_S3_REGION=eu-west-1
  - QUARANTINE_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID=${S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID}
  - QUARANTINE_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=${S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}

  # ----- LLM model routing (single source of truth) ------------------------
  # Each module hard-codes provider-specific model names in its own .env.local
  # (self-hosted/gpt-oss-120b, Qwen/..., bge-m3, gemma-...). The local LiteLLM
  # proxy only serves the models the operator actually configured, so force
  # every module's model variable to one of the three names from the root .env
  # (written by scripts/create_secrets.sh). Module variable names differ, so
  # each is set explicitly; a process ignores variables it does not read, and
  # OS env set here overrides the value in the module's .env.local.
  #   LITELLM_TEXT_MODEL     -> chat / completion
  #   LITELLM_EMBEDDING_MODEL -> text embeddings
  #   LITELLM_VISUAL_MODEL   -> vision / multimodal (image + PDF-page input)
  # Chat:
  - LLM_MODEL=${LITELLM_TEXT_MODEL}
  - LITELLM_MODEL=${LITELLM_TEXT_MODEL}
  - LITELLM_MODEL_NAME=${LITELLM_TEXT_MODEL}
  - MODELS_LARGE_LLM=${LITELLM_TEXT_MODEL}
  - MODELS_MEDIUM_LLM=${LITELLM_TEXT_MODEL}
  - MODELS_SMALL_LLM=${LITELLM_TEXT_MODEL}
  - LLM_DB_RESEARCH_MODEL=${LITELLM_TEXT_MODEL}
  - LLM_PAGEINDEX_SVM_MODEL_STAGE1=${LITELLM_TEXT_MODEL}
  - LLM_PAGEINDEX_SVM_MODEL_STAGE2=${LITELLM_TEXT_MODEL}
  - METADATA_MODEL_NAME=${LITELLM_TEXT_MODEL}
  - STRUCTURE_MODEL_NAME=${LITELLM_TEXT_MODEL}
  - SCHWERPUNKTTHEMA_MODEL_NAME=${LITELLM_TEXT_MODEL}
  - SUMMARIZATION_MODEL_NAME=${LITELLM_TEXT_MODEL}
  # VLM_SUMMARY_MODEL_NAME summarises the *text* output of a prior VLM run -> chat.
  - VLM_SUMMARY_MODEL_NAME=${LITELLM_TEXT_MODEL}
  - LLM_CATEGORISATION_MODEL=${LITELLM_TEXT_MODEL}
  - LLM_SUMMARISATION_MODEL=${LITELLM_TEXT_MODEL}
  - LLM_ENRICHMENT_MODEL=${LITELLM_TEXT_MODEL}
  # Embeddings (plausibilitaet reads LITELLM_EMBEDDING_MODEL directly from .env):
  - EMBEDDING_MODEL=${LITELLM_EMBEDDING_MODEL}
  - LLM_EMBEDDING_MODEL=${LITELLM_EMBEDDING_MODEL}
  - CHUNKING_MODEL=${LITELLM_EMBEDDING_MODEL}
  # Vision / multimodal (modul-inhaltsextraktion: VLM enhancement + LightOnOCR):
  - VLLM_MODEL=${LITELLM_VISUAL_MODEL}
  - LIGHT_ON_OCR_MODEL=${LITELLM_VISUAL_MODEL}

![SPARK Logo](./images/SPARK-Logo.png)

# SPARK Workflow 

Welcome to the repository of the application **SPARK Workflow**!

A detailed description of the project **SPARK** and the features of **SPARK Workflow** can be found on [openCode](https://opencode.de/de/software/spark-workflow-10117). Additional information for public authorities can be found on the [website](https://bmds.bund.de/themen/kuenstliche-intelligenz/ki-in-der-verwaltung/spark) of the BMDS.

For step-by-step guidance on using the application, see the [user manual (DE)](./docs/Benutzerhandbuch_GER_v1.pdf). If you are interested in operating the solution, [the technical product data sheet (DE)](./docs/Technischer_Produktsteckbrief_GER_v1.pdf) is a good starting point. An overview of all documentation in this repository is available in the [documentation index](./docs/README.md).

**SPARK Workflow** was released as open source in consecutive releases. For more information, see [roadmap.md](./docs/roadmap.md).

> [!WARNING]
> Please note the security notice below.

## What it is, what it isn’t

**SPARK Workflow is ...**

* an operational assistance tool for complex administrative planning and permitting procedures. It helps public authorities handle large volumes of application materials, prepare information for review, and support key steps of the procedure.

* based on initial concepts from the use cases of approval procedures for federal highways or hydrogen pipelines (Planfeststellungsverfahren für Bundesfernstraßen oder im Bereich des Wasserstoffkernnetzes). Due to its configurability and modular architecture, it can be adapted to other use cases.

* built to reduce administrative workload while keeping humans in control and accountable. Every AI output has to be actively accepted, edited, or discarded.

* distinctive in embedding AI directly into the authority’s established, legally grounded working process. Results are shown in a user interface designed together with the officials who use it.

**SPARK Workflow is not ...**

* an autonomous system. It supports decision-making but does not decide on its own, and no output takes effect without human review.

* infallible. AI is probabilistic and makes mistakes, just as people do. Which is why human oversight is part of every step.

## Architecture
SPARK Workflow is implemented as a containerized service architecture and is natively designed to run on any Kubernetes-compatible infrastructure. See the [system architecture (GER)](./docs/system-architecture) for more information.

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites

- Docker with Docker Compose
- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)
- [Process Compose](https://f1bonacc1.github.io/process-compose/installation/)
- Node.js 24 and pnpm 10.30.2 for the frontend
- An OpenAI-compatible LLM provider, for example LiteLLM
- A Docling Serve endpoint

### Dependencies

The local development stack provides the shared platform services used by the modules:

- Temporal for workflow execution and the workflow UI
- MinIO/S3 for document and object storage
- Qdrant for vector storage
- PostgreSQL-backed application databases
- Keycloak, SpiceDB, Redis, and the shared backend services configured in Docker Compose and Process Compose

The local setup starts shared infrastructure with Docker Compose and runs the application services, workers, seed jobs, and frontend on the host with Process Compose.

# Quick Start

This guide will walk you through creating your first workflow.

## Prerequisites

- `uv` installed
- `docker` (or any alternative) available
- All services running as outlined in the `README.md` in the repository root

## Steps

1. Start the server

   ```bash
   uv run scripts/quick_start/testrun_ui.py
   ```

2. Open the UI on [`http://localhost:9988/`](http://localhost:9988/)
3. Drop your files into the `uploads` folder (they are gitignored)
4. Then you have two options:
   1. Run a count of files: Set a limit or select all files and click "Run testrun"
   2. Open a dialog with "List Files" and select the specific files you want to use
5. After doing either of these options, you will get two things below. The output of the terminal for debugging purposes and the result of the `upload_testrun.sh` script  
   ![](./docs/assets/output.png)
6. Copy the payload
7. Open [`http://localhost:8080/namespaces/default/workflows/start-workflow`](http://localhost:8080/namespaces/default/workflows/start-workflow)
8. Generate a random UUID
9. Enter `orchestration` into the input for `Task Queue`
10. Enter `IsolatedFVPWorkflow` into the input for `Workflow Type`
11. Paste the payload you just generated into `Data`
12. Verify everything is correct, it should look like this:
    ![](./docs/assets/start_workflow.png)
13. Click `Start Workflow` and look for a green toast to appear in the bottom right corner. This redirects you directly to the workflow you just created

## Notes

The `LLMMatchingWorkflow` will finish quite quickly. This is because there are no document types specified in `document_types.json`. The information that this service expects is outlined in [`05-modulcluster/modul-formale-pruefung/README.md`](../../05-modulcluster/modul-formale-pruefung/README.md)

You can fill in the document types you want in `document_types.json` and the UI will automatically pick these up when you generate a test run.

import re, socket, json, urllib.request

lines=open('process-compose.yaml').read().split('\n')
entries=[]
for i,l in enumerate(lines):
    m=re.match(r'^  ([a-z0-9_\-]+):\s*$', l)
    if m: entries.append((i,m.group(1)))
svc={}
for idx,(start,name) in enumerate(entries):
    end=entries[idx+1][0] if idx+1<len(entries) else len(lines)
    block='\n'.join(lines[start:end])
    port=None
    for m in re.finditer(r'port:\s*(\d+)', block):
        port=int(m.group(1))
    # also catch --port in command
    cm=re.search(r'--port (\d+)', block)
    if cm: port=int(cm.group(1))
    svc[name]=port

# API statuses
ap=json.load(urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:8080/processes'))['data']
status={p['name']:p for p in ap}

def listening(port):
    s=socket.socket(); s.settimeout(1.0)
    try: s.connect(('127.0.0.1',port)); r=True
    except Exception: r=False
    s.close()
    return r

print(f"{'name':32s} {'port':>6s} {'api_status':10s} {'port_up':8s}")
up=down=0
for name in sorted(svc):

    if port:

        flag=''
        if st=='Running' and not l: flag='  <== RUNNING but PORT CLOSED!'
        if st in ('Completed',) and l: flag='  <== completed but port up'
        if st not in ('Completed','') and l: up+=1
        if port and not l and st!='Completed': down+=1
        print(f"{name:32s} {str(port):>6s} {st:10s} {str(l):8s}{flag}")
    else:
        print(f"{name:32s} {'--':>6s} {st:10s} {'--':8s}")
print()
print("Summary: ports OPEN & running:", up, "| ports CLOSED & not-completed:", down)
